title: A Multiline Analysis of the Distribution and Excitation of CS and H<SUB>2</SUB>CS in the HD 163296 Disk
question: How are CS, H2CS and their 34S isotopologues distributed and excited in the HD 163296 disk (rotational temperature, column density, 32S/34S ratio, emitting layer)?

data.bands: ALMA Band 3 to Band 8, plus SMA
data.arrays: ALMA (SB and LB data for 2017.1.01682.S) and SMA compact configuration with 8 antennas
data.angular_resolution: about 0.2-0.4 arcsec (20-40 au) for most lines; coarser for CS 5-4 (SMA) and CS 10-9

what.value: CS J=2-1 image properties and integrated flux

evidence.quote: The image properties and flux for CS J=2–1 are taken from (cite: Oberg21_MAPSI).
The spectroscopic constants for all lines are taken from the CDMS database (cite: Muller01; Muller05; Endres16)

what.value: HD 163296 system parameters (PA, inclination, systemic velocity, stellar mass)

evidence.quote: PA=133.$^{\circ}$3, incl=46.$^{\circ}$7, v$_{\rm{sys}}$=5.8 km s$^{-1}$, and M$_*$=2.0 M$_{\odot}$ (cite: Oberg21_MAPSI; Teague21)

what.value: 2D gas temperature structure T(r,z) of the HD 163296 disk, renormalized for emitting-region inference

evidence.quote: we first renormalized the 2D temperature profile of (cite: Law21_MAPSIV)

what.value: Thermochemical model CO snowline radius used to renormalize the temperature profile

evidence.quote: matches the midplane radius derived in the thermochemical models of (cite: Zhang21)
which is at least several times lower than the ISM ratio of ${\approx}$22 (cite: Wilson99)

what.value: Ortho-to-para ratio measured from H2CO in HD 163296 (2.70 +0.20/-0.19), used to support the adopted value of 3

evidence.quote: which is approximately consistent with the ratio (2.70$^{+0.20}_{-0.19}$) measured from H$_2$CO in the HD 163296 disk (cite: Hernandez_Vera24)

recipe.method: Pipeline calibration by ALMA staff; per-program self-calibration after aligning execution blocks with fixvis/fixplanets; SMA data calibrated with MIR then exported to CASA; some measurement sets obtained pre-calibrated from other authors
key_parameters: CS 3-2: two phase-only rounds (900s, 360s) on SB, then one phase-only round (inf) after concatenating LB; about 2x peak continuum SNR gain
CS 4-3 and H2CS: three phase rounds (inf, 120s, 60s) and one amplitude round (inf)
CS 8-7: two phase rounds (900s, 360s) and one amplitude round (inf) after flagging strong-line channels

recipe.goal: Subtract continuum and image line cubes
recipe.method: uvcontsub (first-order polynomial) then tclean with Briggs weighting, multiscale deconvolver and Keplerian masks, with per-line robust and uv-taper
key_parameters: multiscale pixel scales [0,5,15,25]; CLEAN to 4 sigma, sigma from five line-free channels of the dirty image
velocity binning to channel spacings 0.13-1.20 km/s depending on the line
robust chosen manually to maximize detection SNR

recipe.goal: Make moment maps, radial profiles and integrated fluxes
recipe.method: Zeroth-moment and peak-intensity maps with bettermoments; deprojected radial profiles and spectra with GoFish using the Keplerian masks; flux uncertainties by bootstrapping
key_parameters: no flux threshold for pixel inclusion; same Keplerian masks as CLEANing
uncertainty = standard deviation of fluxes in 500 random Keplerian masks over line-free channels
assumptions: flat (midplane) emitting surface for deprojected radial profiles

recipe.method: LTE rotational diagram with optical depth correction, disk-integrated fluxes from Table 1; H2CS and H2C34S Trot fixed to CS-derived value; ortho-to-para ratio 3 for total column
key_parameters: 256 walkers, 2000 burn-in steps plus 1000 sampling steps; median and 16th/84th percentiles
uniform priors Trot 3-300 K, NT 1e7-1e20 cm^-2
CS and C34S partition function Q(T) = kT/(hB0) + 1/3 with B0 = 24495.56 MHz (CS) and 24103.55 MHz (C34S)
10% flux calibration uncertainty added in quadrature
assumptions: statistical ortho-to-para ratio of 3 for H2CS and H2C34S
thermal line widths, FWHM about 1-2 km/s measured from resolved lines

recipe.method: Beam-matched images (0.35 arcsec for CS/H2CS, 0.5 arcsec for C34S) and the same rotational diagram fit per radius; H2CS and H2C34S use the CS Trot profile
key_parameters: Lines used: CS J=2-1, 3-2, 4-3, 8-7, C34S J=5-4, 6-5, H2CS J=6-5, H2C34S J=9-8; CS J=7-6 excluded for small MRS
C34S priors Trot 10-35 K, NT 1e9-1e17 cm^-2

recipe.goal: Constrain CS emitting height from channel maps
recipe.method: Overlay isovelocity contours at z/r = 0 to 0.2 in steps of 0.05 on CS J=4-3 channel maps and compare by eye; direct surface extraction failed for low SNR

recipe.goal: Infer emitting regions from Trot and 2D gas temperature
recipe.method: Map radially-resolved Trot onto the renormalized 2D T(r,z) of HD 163296 to find the (r,z) region where gas temperature equals Trot

recipe.goal: Test sub-thermal excitation and estimate gap gas density
recipe.method: RADEX calculations at typical CS gap conditions compared Tex and Tkin; sub-thermal excitation assumed significant within a factor 10 of n_crit of CS J=8-7 to estimate gap surface density
key_parameters: critical densities about 1e4 cm^-3 (J=2-1) to 5e6 cm^-3 (J=8-7) at 20-30 K
assumptions: Critical densities from Shirley15; gap at D85 is the planet-carved gap

answer_key.quantity: H2CS disk-integrated column density (Trot fixed to CS)
H2C34S disk-integrated column density (Trot fixed to CS)
N(CS)/N(C34S) using the warmer CS excitation temperature for C34S

evidence.quote: the resulting disk-integrated ratio is N(CS)/N(C$^{34}$S) = 10.4$^{+2.0}_{-1.1}$

answer_key.quantity: Line optical depths range (H2C34S to CS)
CS and C34S ring radii (two rings)

evidence.quote: In general, CS and C$^{34}$S take the form of two rings at radii of ${\approx}$40-50 au and ${\approx}$110-120 au.
H$_2$CS instead shows only a single ring at 56 au
H$_2$C$^{34}$S peaks in a narrower ring at a smaller radius of 37 au
Two external rings at ${\approx}$240 au and ${\approx}$385 au are seen in CS J=4–3
CS is relatively well-constrained to a height of $z/r\lesssim0.1$

answer_key.quantity: Gas surface density at the D85 gap from CS J=8-7 sub-thermal excitation

evidence.loc: 5.2 Local Sub-thermal CS Line Excitation in a Planet-Carved Gap

answer_key.quantity: 32S/34S ratio from CS/C34S and H2CS/H2C34S (disk-averaged and resolved)

not_stated_but_needed: uv-taper sizes for each line (Table 1 only flags 'taper')
image size and cell size for each cube
which channels were line-free for uvcontsub and for the RMS estimate
Keplerian mask parameters other than the maximum radius (e.g. emission surface and width used)
CLEAN niter and mask details beyond the 4 sigma threshold
ALMA flux, bandpass and phase calibrators and pipeline versions for each project
self-calibration details (solints, reference antenna, gaincal parameters) for the C34S data sets obtained privately from other authors
primary beam correction treatment for fluxes and rings
exact method of interpolating CDMS partition functions for H2CS and H2C34S
RADEX inputs (collision partner, density grid, line width) for the sub-thermal excitation check
how the gap gas surface density was converted from n_crit to Sigma_g (scale height, abundance)
renormalization details of the 2D temperature profile
missing_for_reproduction: uv-taper sizes, image and cell sizes per line
pre-calibrated C34S, H2C34S measurement sets from other authors
ALMA calibrator and pipeline details per project
RADEX setup and gas density conversion for the gap estimate
score_reason: Table 1 gives fluxes, beams, robust values and spectroscopy, and the rotational diagram method, priors and sampler settings are explicit, but taper sizes, line-free channels, some self-cal products and RADEX/gap-density details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Data are archival and mostly public, the rotational diagram fits can be redone from tabulated fluxes with stated priors and walkers, and the main results (Trot, NT, ratios, 32S/34S) are numeric; imaging reproduction is less complete.
